subject: Copywriting
title: McDonald's: I'm Lovin' It
description: One-minute skill: McDonald's: I'm Lovin' It.

hook.text: 'I'm Lovin' It' launched in 2003 with a Justin Timberlake jingle. It became McDonald's longest-running slogan ever.

buildup.text: A German agency—Heye & Partner—created the concept.

discovery.text: The 'ba da ba ba bah' jingle became a sonic logo worth billions. People sing it without realizing they're advertising.

twist.text: Critics called it grammatically lazy and unoriginal. But brand recall hit 90%. Academics lost; consumers voted.

climax.text: 20 years later, it's still the tagline. McDonald's has tried to replace it and can't.

punchline.text: Ba da ba ba bah. Four notes worth more than most brands.

quiz.question: In how many countries did 'I'm Lovin' It' launch?

details.summary: McDonald's 'I'm Lovin' It' launched globally in 2003 and became the longest-running slogan in the chain's history. Created by Heye & Partner in Germany and paired with a Justin Timberlake jingle, it replaced a decade of failed slogans and unified the brand's global identity.
details.whyItMatters: This slogan shows how music, language, and global consistency can rescue a struggling brand voice. It proves that simplicity and emotional warmth beat clever wordplay on a global scale.
takeaways: The slogan launched in 2003 and is still in use decades later
A German ad agency created it, proving great copy crosses borders
The 'ba da ba ba ba' jingle became inseparable from the slogan

faq.question: Why did McDonald's use a German agency for a global slogan?
faq.answer: McDonald's held a global competition among 14 agencies. Heye & Partner from Munich won because their concept was emotionally universal and culturally adaptable. The lesson: great ideas can come from anywhere, not just New York or London.

faq.question: How important was the jingle to the slogan's success?
faq.answer: The five-note jingle 'ba da ba ba ba' became a sonic logo as recognizable as the golden arches. Research shows pairing a slogan with a distinctive sound dramatically increases recall. The music made the words unforgettable.
